title: GPU Detail
description: One GPU in depth: live power, utilization, memory, thermals, clocks and what limits them, daily energy, state history, device identity and the health of the metrics path. nvidia_gpu_exporter in nvidia-smi mode (the NVML-only process/ECC/XID/MIG/PCIe-throughput metrics are not produced by this build).

list.name: host
list.label: Box
list.description: GPU box, by the host label vmagent stamps on every sample (listed if seen in the last 30 days).

list.name: gpu
list.label: GPU
list.description: GPU on the selected box: name, index and the first 8 characters of its UUID.

panels.description: Board power draw, 1-minute averages over the last 3 hours; the value is the latest minute.
Share of time at least one kernel was running (nvidia-smi utilization.gpu) -- busy time, not how much of the chip the kernels used. 1-minute averages over the last 3 hours.
Framebuffer memory in use, including whatever the inference engine reserved up front.
GPU die temperature, hottest sample per minute over the last 3 hours (fixed 0-100 C scale).
Degrees Celsius left before the driver's thermal slowdown point (temperature.gpu.tlimit), tightest sample per minute. Amber under 10, red under 5.
Graphics (shader) clock, 1-minute averages; the SM clock tracks it exactly on this card.

Energy since local midnight: a running sum of 5-minute integrate() windows over the raw power samples, each looking one step ahead so the day starts at midnight and the last step reaches now. Short windows matter: a whole-day integrate() range query carries the last reading through an outage (read 27% high for 10 Sep). integrate() wraps the raw selector -- integrate(max(m)[..]) is an implicit subquery that resamples.

What is limiting the clocks right now (any flag in the last 2 minutes), most specific cause first: power brake, HW thermal, SW thermal, the umbrella HW-slowdown flag (NVIDIA: it also fires on P-state changes), SW power cap (the card at its power limit -- normal under full load), or a driver recovery action. Offline = no samples.

targets.expr: max(label_set(max(max_over_time(nvidia_smi_clocks_event_reasons_sw_power_cap{job="gpu",host=~"$host",uuid=~"$gpu"}[2m])) * 1, "r", "1") or label_set(max(max_over_time(nvidia_smi_clocks_event_reasons_hw_slowdown{job="gpu",host=~"$host",uuid=~"$gpu"}[2m])) * 2, "r", "2") or label_set(max(max_over_time(nvidia_smi_clocks_event_reasons_sw_thermal_slowdown{job="gpu",host=~"$host",uuid=~"$gpu"}[2m])) * 3, "r", "3") or label_set(max(max_over_time(nvidia_smi_clocks_event_reasons_hw_thermal_slowdown{job="gpu",host=~"$host",uuid=~"$gpu"}[2m])) * 4, "r", "4") or label_set(max(max_over_time(nvidia_smi_clocks_event_reasons_hw_power_brake_slowdown{job="gpu",host=~"$host",uuid=~"$gpu"}[2m])) * 5, "r", "5") or label_set((max(max_over_time(nvidia_smi_gpu_recovery_action{job="gpu",host=~"$host",uuid=~"$gpu"}[2m])) > bool 0) * 6, "r", "6")) or on() vector(7)

panels.title: Power
panels.description: Board power per step: average (filled) and peak (dotted), against the enforced power limit (dashed). The axis keeps the whole budget in view so idle reads as idle; the peak line keeps short full-load bursts visible at long ranges.

panels.title: Temperature
panels.description: Die temperature (hottest sample per step) against the driver's thermal slowdown point (dashed: temperature + temperature.gpu.tlimit headroom, hour-averaged because the two gauges are sampled a moment apart and jitter by 1 C).

panels.title: Fan
panels.description: Fan duty per step. 0% at idle is the card's zero-RPM mode, not a fault. Its own chart rather than a second axis on Temperature (two y-scales on one plot invent a correlation).

panels.title: Daily Energy (30d)
panels.description: kWh per local day, today last (so far): the sum of 5-minute integrate() windows over the raw power samples, looking FORWARD one day from each local-midnight step (offset -1d; the backward form draws each day on the next day's midnight). Short windows stop a trailing outage from being filled with the last reading -- a whole-day integrate() range query held 1 W from 16:01 to midnight on 10 Sep (0.0366 vs 0.0287 kWh measured).

panels.title: Utilization
panels.description: GPU busy = share of time a kernel was running (utilization.gpu). Memory bandwidth = memory-controller busy time scaled by the memory clock against its maximum (utilization.memory x clock / max clock). The raw utilization.memory counts busy time at the CURRENT clock, so display scan-out on a downclocked idle card read 51% at 405 MHz and 2% at 13.8 GHz -- the scaled line is what fraction of peak bandwidth was actually used. Per-step averages; the product is sampled every 2 minutes (panel min step 2m) so a 30-day view stays under VictoriaMetrics' 100k-points-per-subquery limit (good to ~139 days).

panels.title: VRAM
panels.description: Framebuffer split into used, driver-reserved and free; the stack sums to the card's total memory.

panels.title: Clocks
panels.description: Graphics and memory clocks as a share of each one's maximum (time-averaged per step), on one axis. Absolute values: the Graphics clock card and the Link & Limits table.

panels.title: Clock Limiter & P-State
panels.description: Two rows on one time axis. Clock limiter: the most specific active reason in each step, taking any flag raised within the step (max_over_time) so brief events survive long ranges; a faint band means data but nothing limiting, a gap means no data. P-state: the most common state in each step (mode_over_time) -- time-in-state stays honest (the busiest-state reduction painted P1 over 93% of a day that spent 38% there); P0 = maximum performance, P8+ = idle.

targets.expr: max(label_set(max(max_over_time(nvidia_smi_clocks_event_reasons_sw_power_cap{job="gpu",host=~"$host",uuid=~"$gpu"}[$__interval])) * 1, "r", "1") or label_set(max(max_over_time(nvidia_smi_clocks_event_reasons_hw_slowdown{job="gpu",host=~"$host",uuid=~"$gpu"}[$__interval])) * 2, "r", "2") or label_set(max(max_over_time(nvidia_smi_clocks_event_reasons_sw_thermal_slowdown{job="gpu",host=~"$host",uuid=~"$gpu"}[$__interval])) * 3, "r", "3") or label_set(max(max_over_time(nvidia_smi_clocks_event_reasons_hw_thermal_slowdown{job="gpu",host=~"$host",uuid=~"$gpu"}[$__interval])) * 4, "r", "4") or label_set(max(max_over_time(nvidia_smi_clocks_event_reasons_hw_power_brake_slowdown{job="gpu",host=~"$host",uuid=~"$gpu"}[$__interval])) * 5, "r", "5") or label_set((max(max_over_time(nvidia_smi_gpu_recovery_action{job="gpu",host=~"$host",uuid=~"$gpu"}[$__interval])) > bool 0) * 6, "r", "6"))

panels.title: Throttled
panels.description: How long a specific throttle reason (power cap, SW/HW thermal, power brake) held the clocks over the dashboard range, from the 15-second flags: the flagged share of samples x the range. The driver's cumulative *_seconds counters are not used -- on this box the power-cap counter froze at 235 s while the flag kept firing. The umbrella HW-slowdown flag is left out (it also fires on P-state changes).

panels.title: Device
panels.description: Identity of the selected GPU from nvidia_smi_gpu_info: the newest label set seen in 30 days (topk_max on the last-sample timestamp, so a driver upgrade replaces the old row instead of adding a column).

targets.expr: max by (name, driver_version, cuda_version, vbios_version, compute_cap, driver_model_current, pci_bus_id)(topk_max(1, tlast_over_time(nvidia_smi_gpu_info{job="gpu",host=~"$host",uuid=~"$gpu"}[30d])))

panels.title: Link & Limits
panels.description: Where the card sits against its own ceilings right now: power against the enforced limit, VRAM against capacity, clocks against their maxima, and the PCIe link against what the card supports (a link running narrower than its maximum -- e.g. x8 of x16 -- is set by the slot or riser; it barely matters for inference, where weights stay on the card).

targets.expr: label_set(round(round(max(nvidia_smi_power_draw_watts{job="gpu",host=~"$host",uuid=~"$gpu"})), 0.1), "item", "Power (W)", "o", "1") or label_set(round(max(nvidia_smi_memory_used_bytes{job="gpu",host=~"$host",uuid=~"$gpu"}) / 1073741824, 0.1), "item", "VRAM (GiB)", "o", "2") or label_set(round(max(nvidia_smi_clocks_current_graphics_clock_hz{job="gpu",host=~"$host",uuid=~"$gpu"}) / 1e6, 0.1), "item", "Graphics clock (MHz)", "o", "3") or label_set(round(max(nvidia_smi_clocks_current_memory_clock_hz{job="gpu",host=~"$host",uuid=~"$gpu"}) / 1e6, 0.1), "item", "Memory clock (MHz)", "o", "4") or label_set(round(max(nvidia_smi_pcie_link_gen_current{job="gpu",host=~"$host",uuid=~"$gpu"}), 0.1), "item", "PCIe generation", "o", "5") or label_set(round(max(nvidia_smi_pcie_link_width_current{job="gpu",host=~"$host",uuid=~"$gpu"}), 0.1), "item", "PCIe lanes", "o", "6")

label_set(round(max(nvidia_smi_enforced_power_limit_watts{job="gpu",host=~"$host",uuid=~"$gpu"}), 0.1), "item", "Power (W)", "o", "1") or label_set(round(max(nvidia_smi_memory_total_bytes{job="gpu",host=~"$host",uuid=~"$gpu"}) / 1073741824, 0.1), "item", "VRAM (GiB)", "o", "2") or label_set(round(max(nvidia_smi_clocks_max_graphics_clock_hz{job="gpu",host=~"$host",uuid=~"$gpu"}) / 1e6, 0.1), "item", "Graphics clock (MHz)", "o", "3") or label_set(round(max(nvidia_smi_clocks_max_memory_clock_hz{job="gpu",host=~"$host",uuid=~"$gpu"}) / 1e6, 0.1), "item", "Memory clock (MHz)", "o", "4") or label_set(round(max(nvidia_smi_pcie_link_gen_max{job="gpu",host=~"$host",uuid=~"$gpu"}), 0.1), "item", "PCIe generation", "o", "5") or label_set(round(max(nvidia_smi_pcie_link_width_max{job="gpu",host=~"$host",uuid=~"$gpu"}), 0.1), "item", "PCIe lanes", "o", "6")

label_set((round(max(nvidia_smi_power_draw_watts{job="gpu",host=~"$host",uuid=~"$gpu"}))) / (max(nvidia_smi_enforced_power_limit_watts{job="gpu",host=~"$host",uuid=~"$gpu"})), "item", "Power (W)", "o", "1") or label_set((max(nvidia_smi_memory_used_bytes{job="gpu",host=~"$host",uuid=~"$gpu"}) / 1073741824) / (max(nvidia_smi_memory_total_bytes{job="gpu",host=~"$host",uuid=~"$gpu"}) / 1073741824), "item", "VRAM (GiB)", "o", "2") or label_set((max(nvidia_smi_clocks_current_graphics_clock_hz{job="gpu",host=~"$host",uuid=~"$gpu"}) / 1e6) / (max(nvidia_smi_clocks_max_graphics_clock_hz{job="gpu",host=~"$host",uuid=~"$gpu"}) / 1e6), "item", "Graphics clock (MHz)", "o", "3") or label_set((max(nvidia_smi_clocks_current_memory_clock_hz{job="gpu",host=~"$host",uuid=~"$gpu"}) / 1e6) / (max(nvidia_smi_clocks_max_memory_clock_hz{job="gpu",host=~"$host",uuid=~"$gpu"}) / 1e6), "item", "Memory clock (MHz)", "o", "4") or label_set((max(nvidia_smi_pcie_link_gen_current{job="gpu",host=~"$host",uuid=~"$gpu"})) / (max(nvidia_smi_pcie_link_gen_max{job="gpu",host=~"$host",uuid=~"$gpu"})), "item", "PCIe generation", "o", "5") or label_set((max(nvidia_smi_pcie_link_width_current{job="gpu",host=~"$host",uuid=~"$gpu"})) / (max(nvidia_smi_pcie_link_width_max{job="gpu",host=~"$host",uuid=~"$gpu"})), "item", "PCIe lanes", "o", "6")

panels.title: Exporter
panels.description: Health of the metrics path on the GPU box, evaluated now: the vmagent scrape of the exporter and the exporter's last nvidia-smi call (vmagent runs on the box, so an outage leaves no samples at all -- missing reads DOWN / FAILING), how long the call took, failed scrapes over the dashboard range, and how old the newest GPU sample is.
